issues.legal_issue: Eyewitness testimony may be accepted despite minor discrepancies and superficial injuries where it is straightforward and corroborated by other witnesses and the medical evidence.
material_facts: The prosecution witnesses were present at the scene, and one was an injured witness who gave a prompt report containing the essential details.
The injured witness had minor injuries consistent with her account of the occurrence.
The other eyewitnesses corroborated her account, including the attribution of the fatal blows to one assailant.
The discrepancies identified by the trial court concerned minor details, and the court found no exaggeration or false implication.
issues.conclusion: The eyewitness evidence was reliable, and the trial court's reasons for rejecting it were unsound; the evidence supported the convictions that the High Court had entered, including those of the assailant who inflicted the fatal blows.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the eyewitness evidence against the witnesses' presence at the scene, its consistency and corroboration, and the medical evidence. It held that minor discrepancies and superficial injuries did not justify rejecting the straightforward, corroborated account. No earlier cases or specific statutory provisions were relied on for this evidentiary determination.

rule.if: appeal_following_reversal_of_acquittal and eyewitnesses_present_at_scene and testimony_corroborated and discrepancies_minor

predicates.appeal_following_reversal_of_acquittal: The case is an appeal following a higher court's reversal of an acquittal.
predicates.eyewitnesses_present_at_scene: Witnesses who testified to the occurrence were present where it happened.
predicates.testimony_corroborated: The account of an eyewitness was supported by other eyewitnesses or by medical evidence.
predicates.discrepancies_minor: The differences in the witnesses' accounts concerned details rather than the central events.

issues.definition: When an appeal follows reversal of an acquittal and eyewitnesses present at the scene give corroborated testimony with only minor discrepancies, the eyewitness evidence is accepted.

issues.legal_issue: A participant who did not share an intention to kill cannot be held liable for murder with common intention merely because another participant inflicted the fatal injuries.
material_facts: One accused inflicted the fatal blows on both deceased persons.
The other accused helped pull one deceased person down and inflicted only simple injuries with a stick.
The evidence did not establish that the latter accused shared an intention to kill.
issues.conclusion: The murder convictions of the accused who did not share the intention to kill, under Sections 302 read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code, were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 302 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, murder liability with common intention required proof that the accused shared the intention to kill. The Court found that the limited acts attributed to this accused did not establish that common intention. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: appeal_from_murder_conviction_with_common_intention and another_participant_inflicted_fatal_blow and accused_inflicted_only_simple_injuries and shared_intention_to_kill_not_established

predicates.appeal_from_murder_conviction_with_commo: The proceeding is an appeal from a murder conviction based on common intention.
predicates.another_participant_inflicted_fatal_blow: A different participant inflicted the fatal injury or injuries.
predicates.accused_inflicted_only_simple_injuries: The accused's own acts caused only simple injuries and did not include a fatal blow.
predicates.shared_intention_to_kill_not_established: The evidence did not establish that the accused shared an intention to kill.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a murder conviction based on common intention, if another participant inflicted the fatal blow, the accused inflicted only simple injuries, and a shared intention to kill was not established, the murder conviction with common intention is set aside.

issues.legal_issue: An accused who inflicted a simple injury on a deceased person could be convicted under Section 324 of the Indian Penal Code in this case.
material_facts: The accused inflicted one simple injury on one deceased person with a stick.
The Supreme Court distinguished that act from the fatal blows inflicted by another accused.
issues.conclusion: The Court convicted the accused under Section 324 of the Indian Penal Code for the injury to the deceased and imposed a term of rigorous imprisonment.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Section 324 of the Indian Penal Code to the accused's infliction of one simple injury on the deceased. It did not cite any earlier case or provide a further explanation of the provision's application.

predicates.appeal_involving_assault_on_deceased: The proceeding concerns criminal liability for an assault on a person who died in the incident.
predicates.accused_inflicted_simple_injury_with_sti: The accused inflicted a simple injury on the deceased using a stick.
predicates.accused_did_not_inflict_fatal_blow: The accused did not inflict the fatal injury.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning an assault on a deceased person, where the accused inflicted a simple injury with a stick but not the fatal blow, the accused is convicted for the hurt under the offense applied by the Court.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction for voluntarily causing hurt may be sustained where the accused struck an eyewitness and the evidence supported that injury.
material_facts: The accused struck the widow of one deceased person with a stick.
She warded off the blow with her hands and sustained an injury to her hand.
Her account of the occurrence and the injuries was accepted.
issues.conclusion: The conviction under Section 323 of the Indian Penal Code for causing hurt to the eyewitness was confirmed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court confirmed the conviction under Section 323 of the Indian Penal Code on the accepted evidence that the accused caused hurt to the eyewitness. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: appeal_from_hurt_conviction and accused_struck_witness and witness_sustained_hurt and injury_evidence_accepted

predicates.appeal_from_hurt_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal from a conviction for causing hurt.
predicates.accused_struck_witness: The accused struck a person who witnessed the occurrence.
predicates.witness_sustained_hurt: The person struck sustained an injury.
predicates.injury_evidence_accepted: The evidence establishing the injury and the accused's act was accepted.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a hurt conviction, if the accused struck a witness, the witness sustained hurt, and the injury evidence was accepted, the conviction for voluntarily causing hurt is confirmed.

issues.legal_issue: A conviction for attempt to murder with common intention may be affirmed while the sentence is reduced.
material_facts: One injured witness sustained several contusions and a lacerated wound, and medical examination disclosed fractures in the arm and hand bones.
The High Court had convicted both accused under Section 307 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code for causing injuries to that witness.
The Supreme Court confirmed the conviction but reduced one accused's sentence.
issues.conclusion: The conviction under Section 307 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code was confirmed, while the sentence imposed on the accused whose appeal was allowed in part was reduced.
issues.legal_principle: The Court confirmed the conviction under Sections 307 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code and reduced the sentence. The judgment gives no separate explanation for the sentence reduction and cites no earlier cases for it.

predicates.appeal_from_attempt_to_murder_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal from an attempt-to-murder conviction based on common intention.
predicates.injured_witness_sustained_multiple_injur: The injured witness sustained multiple wounds or contusions.
predicates.medical_evidence_showed_fractures: Medical examination disclosed fractures in the injured witness.

issues.definition: In an appeal from an attempt-to-murder conviction based on common intention, if the injured witness sustained multiple injuries and medical evidence showed fractures, the conviction is confirmed and the sentence is reduced.
